feed.title: Re: Safer sighashes and more granular SIGHASH_NOINPUT

entry.title: Re: Safer sighashes and more granular SIGHASH_NOINPUT
entry.summary:
A proposal has been introduced to use a 64-byte signature for the default "signing all" sighash type, while retaining a 65-byte signature for other sighash types. This adjustment is anticipated to create space efficiencies, enabling more transactions to fit within each block, which presents an overall gain in transaction throughput.
However, implementing this change introduces complications in accurately estimating witness weight, particularly in multisignature scenarios. The challenge intensifies with complex scripts, where precise weight estimation becomes essential, yet also most difficult. In such cases, although the proposed modification may be effective for straightforward scripts, it may fall short when dealing with intricate ones that actually require accurate witness size predictions.
There are ongoing concerns regarding unavoidable witness size malleability within certain scripting examples. Identifying concrete script instances where witness size malleability cannot be avoided would help clarify the limitations of the proposal and inform further improvements or alternative approaches.
